newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan opposition calls one-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan opposition calls one-day strike.

text.p: Pakistani opposition parties said on Wednesday they would back a one-day strike to protest against the killing of Murtaza Bhutto, estranged brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.
Murtaza, 42, was shot dead on Friday in a gunbattle between Karachi police and his supporters, seven of whom also died.

A spokeswoman for the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) said 10 opposition parties, including the MQM, had decided to support the strike called for Thursday by Murtaza's splinter faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party.
Strikes supported by the MQM have in the past proved effective in Karachi and other cities of the southern province of Sindh, where the movement has its power base.
Murtaza's supporters have accused the police of deliberately killing their leader in an ambush. Police say his bodyguards fired first when they tried to stop his convoy for checks.
